Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:87: And in this same wording it also appears in the Tikkunim (page 26a; cf. page 9a), more explicitly, where it explains that the laying of tefillin benefits even the wicked, to subdue the accusers for him, in these words: for the wicked, they are a binding for all their accusers - behold, the property of tefillin is to subdue the husks. And there is a second intent in laying tefillin for one who is righteous or intermediate, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:88: And as for us, would that we might be at the level of the intermediate ones, for Rabbah called himself intermediate (Berachot 61b), as we copied in the Gate of Fear, end of chapter 6 - it is good for us to lay tefillin all day, so that the husks be subdued by us, and the straps become ropes for the horns of Samael, and so on - for although our intent in laying tefillin above is to unify, as we shall explain, each one's spiritual effect operates according to the merit of his soul: if he is completely righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, will be bound to him in love, and his soul bound up with his soul, as explained in the teaching; but for us, even though we direct the intent stated, the Holy One, blessed be He, will not be bound to us in love, but the commandment will operate upon us only to subdue the husks.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:89: Now, because of the greatness of the virtue of the commandment of tefillin and its properties, which we have explained and shall explain further, with God's help, a person should arouse his heart and soul with love in fulfilling this commandment, in a manner that his mind not stray from them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:90: The things that arouse love through this commandment, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (page 21b), in these words: and should you say that the Holy One, blessed be He, is not bound to her because of this, the verse says (Proverbs 27:8), "like a bird wandering from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his place" - in order to guard her in exile from a foreign dominion, this is what is written (Isaiah 42:8), "I am the LORD, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another," and so on - "to another" is "another god," this is Samael, "to graven images," these are the appointees over the seventy nations - and for her sake the Holy One, blessed be He, is a king bound in the running channels, and He is imprisoned with them in the hand-tefillin, in the knot of the hand - and this is what is written (Ezekiel 24:17), "bind your headdress upon you" - and because He is imprisoned with them in exile, it is said of Him, "no prisoner can free himself from prison," and the Shechinah is His prison, for the sake of His love for her He is bound to her - and the secret of the matter is (Song of Songs 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:91: Now, from the whole of his words there is an exposition for our intent - that when one contemplates that the Holy One, blessed be He, who is King of the universe, is bound with the son of man, formed from a putrid drop, and rests within the running channels of the brain, and this resembles His contracting His Shechinah between the poles of the Ark, even though the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him - therefore it is fitting that the thought of the soul dwelling in his brain cleave to His blessed love, which rests in the brain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:92: And so he explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach, page 175b), that the tefillin are witnesses testifying to a person that the Holy One, blessed be He, cleaves to him, in these words: Rabbi Yehudah said, how many witnesses did the Holy One, blessed be He, make to testify concerning people, and they all stand at his advice and testimony over against him. He rises in the morning and stretches out his feet to walk, witnesses stand against him and proclaim and say (1 Samuel 2:9), "He shall guard the feet of His pious ones." He lays tefillin upon his head, between his eyes, he must lift his head and see the holy supernal Name attached and marked upon his head, and straps hang from this side and that side over his heart, behold he has looked at the glory of his Master. He stretches out his hand and sees the other hand being bound with the binding of the holy Name, he turns his hand and gazes at the glory of his Master - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:93: Behold, it is explicit that the tefillin are witnesses to testify to a person so that he not sin, so that when he wishes to raise his eyes to see what is unfitting, and likewise with his hands, he will remember that the tefillin are on his head and arm, and he will fear the King who dwells with him. And he said, "he sees the holy supernal Name attached and marked upon his head" - the word "attached" means that literally the supernal holiness, from above downward, is attached to him and does not separate from him, along the lines of what we said above, that concerning the tefillin it is said (Exodus 25:8), "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:94: Let us return to the teaching of the Tikkunim - it says at the end of the teaching, "and the Shechinah is His prison, for the sake of His love for her He is bound to her." This is the aspect of the hand-tefillin, for the reality of the four passages that are in the hand-tefillin are Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, as Rashbi explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of page 263) - it follows that this is the secret of the male, bound in the house of the hand, and the house in which the passages are, which is the Shechinah, is His prison, and for love of her He is bound with her - and therefore the Shechinah says, "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts," and this corresponds to the aspect of the hand-tefillin on the arm - and this is "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:95: And this resembles what she says (Song of Songs 8:6), "set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm," and it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 65b) that this is said of the head- and hand-tefillin, in these words: "set me as a seal upon your heart" - who has ever seen a seal upon the heart? Rather, these are the head-tefillin, whose straps hang down upon the heart, and these are the head-tefillin; and the hand-tefillin, which is on the left, opposite the heart - and this is "as a seal upon your heart." "As a seal upon your arm" is the hand-tefillin, for they are the mark of the holy Name, which is Yud - "sanctify to Me every firstborn"; Heh - "and it shall be when he brings you"; Vav - "hear O Israel"; Heh - "and it shall be if you diligently hearken" - and from that mark all the nations of the world tremble, this is what is written (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" - and so they established, "the Name of the LORD" refers to the head-tefillin - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:96: And similarly to this, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Unity, introduction) concerning the explanation of the passage "and you shall love," that all the things mentioned in the passage, such as (Deuteronomy 6:7), "and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and speak of them" - all of them arouse love, and he said afterward, "and you shall bind them for a sign," and so on, and wrote, in these words: and then it moves from the duties of the limbs to the hand-tefillah and the head-tefillah and the mezuzah, and all of them cause one to remember the Creator and love Him with a whole heart, and finally he wears it as a statute of remembrance of the love of lovers, "set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm," and so on, and it says (ibid. 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:97: And what he said in the teaching, "and for her sake the Holy One, blessed be He, is a king bound in the running channels," and so on - this can be understood from what they said in the Tikkunim (page 100b), whose wording we copied in the Gate of Love, chapter 9, that the tefillin are called a garment to hide the Shechinah from the external forces. And through this may be understood what they said in the Talmud (Shabbat 49a), that the tefillin are called "the wings of a dove," concerning Elisha, master of the wings, and it is written (Psalms 68:14), "the wings of a dove covered with silver," and it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 102a) that the thread of Chesed, which is silver, covers and hides the Shechinah and the soul from the masters of judgment - and this is a great property that tefillin have, beyond all that has been expounded.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:98: And so it is further explained in the Tikkunim (end of page 143a), in these words: there are sins for which they judge the soul with severe judgments, but the commandment, which is the Matronita - such as the commandment of tefillin - comes and shields it and spreads its wings over it, and no accuser has permission to draw near there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:99: And among the things that arouse love in this commandment is when one considers that the tefillin we lay, although they are tefillin of leather, in their supernal place are tefillin of light - and this is the secret of what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 84a) and in the Zohar, that the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin, meaning that Tiferet is crowned with supernal lights, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 262b) - and had Adam not sinned, or had Israel not sinned with the calf, they would have been refined like angels, and would have merited tefillin of light. But after the sin, Israel merited only tefillin of leather - meaning the contraction of the supernal lights into the world of Metatron, in which is the secret of exile, in the days of the week, and in it are tefillin of leather, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 264b), that concerning the tefillin it is said (Genesis 3:21), "and the LORD God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin [or]" - in these words: Rabbi Abba sent to Rabbi Shimon, saying to him, that which they established concerning the tefillin of the Master of the universe, that they are the holiness of holinesses, the hide upon the tefillin and the straps are called holiness - from where do we derive this? He sent back to him: "and the LORD God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin," precisely - and so Rav Hamnuna Sabba established it, and these are the head and arm, Yud-Dalet-Kaf-Heh in Heh - and so they established - to this point. And it is known that this verse, "and the LORD God made," is a repair after the sin of the first man, and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 10b), in these words: at first, garments of light [or with an alef], through which he would dim the orb of the sun, being the Creator of the lights of fire - after they sinned, "and the LORD God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin [or with an ayin]" - to this point, relevant here - and this wording is understood in light of what we have already introduced.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:100: And in the Tikkunim (ibid., page 113, chapter 2) they explained the matter explicitly, in these words: after Adam below thought of repentance, the garment returned to the brain, which is the skull of the tefillin, and the brain, which is Chokhmah, joined with Imma, immediately, "and the LORD God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them," and these are the tefillin, which are of skin. At that time, teshuvah, which is Imma, the skull of the tefillin, arose with Adam to shield him and cover him, for he was naked, in the manner that it covers the supernal brain - and therefore, whoever lays tefillin is as though he covers the supernal brain - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:101: And when a person contemplates what we have explained, his heart shall be kindled with love for the Creator, who had compassion on him and contracted the supernal lights into him, clothed in tefillin of leather - and this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, mentioned in the Song of Songs concerning the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel (Song of Songs 7:6), "a king bound in the running channels [rehatim]," which are the head-tefillin, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:102: And by laying tefillin, a person is a complete person, resembling his Creator, as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 83b), in these words: (Genesis 1:27), "and God created man in His image, in the image of God He created him" - here is the precept of tefillin. Come and see, whoever lays tefillin upon his head and his arm, a voice ascends every day to all the living creatures, chariots, ofanim, seraphim, and angels appointed over prayers: give honor to the image of the King, who is one who lays tefillin, of whom it is said, "and God created man in His image, in the image of God He created him." "In His image" - through the head-tefillin, in the manner of the tefillin of the Master of the universe, which are the supernal Shechinah, tefillin upon the head, which is the central pillar, comprising the first three sefirot, and the central pillar comprises six sefirot; and the supernal Mother is tefillin upon His head - these are the tefillin that the Holy One, blessed be He, lays every day. The hand-tefillin is the lower Shechinah, bound to Him, and of her it is said (Genesis 44:30), "and his soul is bound up with his soul" - the two of them in one union, in one binding. The strap wound on the left finger is her betrothal, being the ring wound on her finger, and by it she is bound to Him and He to her - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:103: Behold, it is explained in this teaching the virtue of one who lays tefillin, that he resembles his Creator, and it is somewhat explained in the teaching the intent of the tefillin, to be explained further, with God's help. And incidentally it is explained that the strap we wind on the finger is the ring of betrothal that the male gives her - and from here my teacher, peace be upon him, would say that it is not proper to wind the strap on the finger before laying the head-tefillah, which is the secret of the male - for if the male has not yet come, from where would the betrothal be? And so is the custom of most of Israel, and it is not proper to change the custom. And so my teacher, peace be upon him, would say that this winding on the finger must be done standing, for the male who betroths the woman betroths her standing, since betrothal is from the world of the male, and its manner is standing. And the windings must be three, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 228b), whose wording we copied above concerning the number of windings in the tzitzit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:104: And further, concerning the virtue of one who lays tefillin and tzitzit, they elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 81a), and said that one who lays tefillin and tzitzit is one, resembling his Creator, and since he resembles his Creator, there is a relation and closeness for the Holy One, blessed be He, to rest upon him - but if he does not resemble his Creator, what relation is there for the Holy One, blessed be He, with him? In these words: "you shall be holy" (Leviticus 19:2) - Rabbi Abba opened, "and who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth" (1 Chronicles 17:21). Come and see, among all the nations of the world the Holy One, blessed be He, did not desire any but Israel alone, and He made them one nation, and called them one nation in His own Name, and crowned them with several crowns, with several precepts, to be crowned with them - and therefore, the head-tefillin and the arm-tefillin, for a person to be crowned with them in the manner above, and to be found one, complete in everything - and at that hour when a person is crowned with them and sanctified through them, he becomes complete and is called one, for "one" is called such only when it is complete, and whoever is blemished is not called one - and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is called one in the completeness of everything, in the completeness of the Patriarchs, in the completeness of the Community of Israel - therefore Israel below are called one, for when a person lays tefillin and is covered with the covering of the commandment, then he is crowned with holy crowns in the manner above and is called one - and therefore let one who is one come and occupy himself with the One, the Holy One, blessed be He, who is one, shall occupy Himself with the one - for a king occupies himself only with what is fitting for him - and therefore it is written (Job 23:13), "and He is one, and who can turn Him back" - the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells and is found only in one. "In one" - it should have said simply "one" - but rather in the one who is repaired with supernal holiness to become one - then He dwells in the one and nowhere else. And when is a person called one? At the hour when he is sanctified with supernal crowns - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells and is found only in the one - namely, after a person is repaired with tzitzit and tefillin, for then he is one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:105: If so, at the time a person is occupied with Torah or with prayer, when he wishes the Holy One, blessed be He, to rest with him - if he is blemished and lacks the vessel and ornaments of holiness, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon him, as they said above, "and whoever is blemished is not called one." And it is possible that this is the blessing over tefillin, in saying "who has sanctified us with His commandments" - according to the plain meaning, that since a person wishes to cleave to Him, blessed be He, it is fitting that he first be sanctified with His commandments, and through this there will be a preparation for all supernal holiness to rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:106: And concerning the intent of laying tefillin, I shall copy what is found in the Zohar and the Tikkunim in scattered places, one here and one there, and let the understanding one understand. They said, of blessed memory (Parashat Metzora, page 55a): whoever lays tefillin, when he lays the hand-tefillah, he must extend his left arm to receive the Community of Israel, and to bind the knot with the right, in order to embrace her, to fulfill what is written (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head, and his right embraces me" - so that a person appears in the manner above and is crowned with everything, and then the person is complete in supernal holiness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him (Isaiah 49:3), "Israel, in whom I am glorified" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:107: And when he lays the head-tefillah, and so on, he should stand, corresponding to the world of the male - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 132b), that everything from the world of the male must be done standing and erect. And see further there (Parashat Terumah, beginning of page 133) concerning holiness standing and sitting - and concerning this they said in the Talmud (Sanhedrin 42a): Rabbi Yishmael said, had Israel merited nothing but to greet the countenance of their Father in Heaven once every month, it would be enough for them. Abaye said, therefore it must be said standing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:108: And in laying the hand-tefillah, he should join the knot of the yud with the box, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 236b), in these words: this yud must not depart at all from the hand-tefillah, so as not to cause separation, and all her joy is in this - the yud is in the male and not in the female, and therefore she is drawn near to him, and whoever distances himself from this place is distanced from the delight of the World to Come in the male - he is Tzaddik and she is Tzedek without a yud, he is "ish" [man] and she is "ishah" [woman] without a yud - and therefore his joy is to draw near to her and delight with her; whoever distances this delight, they distance him from the delight above - and concerning this it is written (1 Samuel 2:30), "for those who honor Me I will honor," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:109: And in the intent of the hand- and head-tefillah, one should intend, in the hand-tefillah, that the four passages are the Name YHVH, as explained above: "sanctify [kadesh]" - Yud; "and it shall be when he brings you" - Heh; "hear O Israel" - Vav; "and it shall be if you diligently hearken" - Heh; and the box is the Name Adonai. And in the head-tefillah, the four passages are the Name YHVH in the four boxes, [which are] the Name Ehyeh - so they explained in the Tikkunim (page 9a), in these words: then you shall call and YHVH shall answer (Isaiah 58:9) - YHVH is in the four boxes of the head-tefillin, which are the four letters Ehyeh; "and YHVH shall answer" - YHVH is in the four boxes of the hand-tefillin, which are Adonai. And should you say, are they not in one hand, in one box, and so on - to this point, relevant here. And so they explained in the Tikkunim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:110: And further, in the Tikkunim (page 144b), in these words: (Song of Songs 6:10) "your head upon you is like Carmel" - this is the head-tefillin, and the straps hang from here like tendrils that are like Carmel hanging from a vine. "And the locks of your head like purple [argaman]" - this is the hand-tefillah, that which was like a poor door in exile, this is what is written (Psalms 102:1), "a prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed" - it shall be a garment like purple [argaman], which is the secret of Uriel, Refael, Gabriel, Michael, Nuriel. "A king bound in the running channels" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He, YHVH, who is bound in her four boxes, which are Adonai, the four running channels of the brain - that He be bound in the running channels in this manner, Yud-Aleph-Kaf-Dalet-Vav-Nun-Kuf-Yud [YAKDONKI], "for Your Name is in you and your name is in Him" - and this is the secret of "Amen" from "Argaman" - to this point. And at the end of the teaching, concerning "a king bound in the running channels," it agrees with the previous teaching - and the general rule is that the hand-tefillah is the head of the female, and the running channels of the brain within her are the Name Adonai; and the strap of the hand is what he said, "and the locks" - "your head" alludes to the hair of her head, until "purple," as explained in the teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:111: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of page 263), concerning the intent of laying tefillin, in these words: Rabbi Yitzchak taught, the supernal holy chariot is the four boxes of the tefillin that one lays, being Vav, as has been said; the other holy chariot is the other four, comprised in one, that one lays, being the final Heh, as they established. And it is written further there (page 264, end of page a, in a gloss) - and this is the wording of the glossator: the head-tefillin are Chokhmah and Binah, Gedullah, Gevurah, Tiferet of the one who lays them. And the arm-tefillin are Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut of the one who lays them - to this point. And let it not trouble you what is explained in the Tikkunim, that the four passages are the Name YHVH, for the intent is that Vav inclines to the right, Chesed, and Heh inclines to the left, Gevurah - so my teacher, peace be upon him, explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:112: And before putting on the tefillin, one should say: I am putting on tefillin to fulfill the commandment of my Creator, "and you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes" - the four passages that are in the hand, one should intend that they correspond to the Name YHVH clothed within the Name Adonai, which is the box, and the twenty-one mentions [of the divine Name] within it correspond to the Name Ehyeh. And in the head, they are the four passages of YHVH, and the four boxes of Ehyeh, and further, the Name Ehyeh within it corresponds to the twenty-one mentions - and one should intend to subdue the maidservant under her mistress, and so on, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:113: And concerning the intent of the mentions in the tefillin, which are Ehyeh, twenty-one in the hand and twenty-one in the head, which total forty-two, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 3a), in these words: "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh" within the tefillin, in the twenty-one mentions of the head-tefillin and the twenty-one mentions of the hand-tefillin - and this we call the supernal Mother, the tefillin of the Master of the universe; tefillin upon the head of the central pillar, "Hear O Israel" - the supernal Mother covers Him with her wings, which are the straps of the tefillin - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:114: And by the plain meaning, one must intend the passages themselves written in the tefillin, and through this his heart is aroused to love. In the first two passages, "Kadesh" and "Vehayah ki yeviacha," which correspond to Yud-Heh, one should think of what is written in them, namely the matter of the exodus from Egypt, which indicates the strength of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love, that He Himself went to bring them out from there and slew their firstborn - a parable, of a king whose son was captive, and the king himself went, for love of his son, and brought him out from there by force, and waged war with his captor. So the Holy One, blessed be He, in His own glory and by Himself - He, and not an angel and not a seraph, slew their firstborn and brought them out, as it says (Exodus 12:29), "and the LORD struck every firstborn" - and this is what Moses warns Israel (ibid. 13:3), "remember this day on which you went out from Egypt," and so on, "for with a strong hand the LORD brought you out from there," and so on - and the word "remember" is an infinitive, for we are forever obligated to remember this matter, so that we remember His love in our hearts and serve Him like a son who loves his father because of the good He did for him - and this is why Scripture calls us sons, as it says (ibid. 4:22), "Israel is My firstborn son" - and the intent is concerning the holy soul that flowed to us from the place of holiness, from where the firstborn is holy, and therefore it says (ibid. 13:2), "sanctify to Me every firstborn" - and because of this we are obligated to sanctify ourselves so that we cleave to Him, and this matter is what is written in the second passage, and in it is explained further the matter of the slaying of the firstborn, in saying (ibid. 13:15), "and the LORD slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast" - and in these two passages He informs us of the matter of providence and power, for He overturned the arrangements of the heavens and broke the iron bars, as explained in the Zohar, and so it is written (Deuteronomy 4:20), "and you the LORD has taken and brought out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be to Him a people of inheritance."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:115: And in the two passages "Shema" and "Vehayah im shamoa," He reminds us of the unity of the LORD, namely that YHVH is one above and below and in the four directions of the world, which we saw at the standing at Mount Sinai, as explained in chapter 1 of the Gate of Fear - and afterward He warns us concerning love, and that we should make signs for the reality of love, so that His love not depart from our hearts, and "these words that I command you today" concern the matter of love and unity upon your heart, "and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and speak of them when you sit in your house," and so on, "and you shall bind them for a sign," so that we remember love and unity - and this matter is written in the passage "Vehayah im shamoa," "to love," and so on, except that He forewarns us that if our heart is enticed after the evil inclination, which is "other gods," "then the anger [of the LORD will be kindled]," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:116: And concerning the straps of the head, and the knot of the head-tefillin and the hand-tefillin, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 236b), in these words: two straps go out from this side and that side, of the two thighs of this "Aleph" of "Chet" [the letter shapes], to which the true prophets cling, for from above two arms go out, from the right and from the left, and the Dalet is attached to them; afterward the thighs spread downward - once she is attached above properly, she descends below to be attached to her hosts; when she is attached, she takes hold of the lower parts of the thighs, and the mark of the yud, the holy supernal covenant, is from above, then she is attached in unity - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:117: Further, concerning the hand-strap, it says in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of page 263), in these words: and therefore, from this one strap hangs down, for from her the lower beings hang and are nourished from her, and therefore she is called "a sign," as it is said (Genesis 9:12), "this is the sign of the covenant," and it is written (Exodus 13:16), "and it shall be for a sign upon your hand," with Yud-Kaf-Heh in Heh - and so they established.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:118: Further, concerning the secret of the straps, they explained, of blessed memory (Tikkunei Zohar, page 9b): three straps are Netzach, Hod, Yesod - Yesod is the strap that binds Vav with Heh, for "everything is in the heavens and on earth" [Chronicles], attached to heaven and earth. Two straps, Netzach and Hod, attached to the supernal Heh, and the horns are high, one higher than the other - so too the two straps, one long and one short. The short one to the chest, the long one to the navel. And the spreading of the supernal Heh to Hod is in the letter Yud, which is the knot of the head-tefillin, for the supernal Heh ascends to fifty - five times ten in the letter Yud - and this is from the Heh-Yud of "Elohim," five times Heh in the letter Yud, fifty in the five sefirot. Yesod, "kol" [all], takes them all and inherits them all for the bride, and this is "kol kallah" [all the bride]. In the letter Heh below, one horn - and the secret of the matter, our Rabbis established, that the ox that Adam the first man offered had one horn on its forehead, as it is said (Psalms 69:32), "more than a bull with horns [makrin]" - "makren" lacking a yud - and this is the hand-strap of the tefillin of the Master of the universe - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:119: And concerning the secret of the "shin"s on the tefillin, it says in the Tikkunim (page 9a), in these words: the "shin" of the tefillin is a law given to Moses at Sinai - a "shin" of three heads, a "shin" of four heads, corresponding to the seven maidens fitting to be given her from the king's house, which are, in the morning, two before her and one after her, and in the evening, two before her and two after her (Berachot, chapter 1, mishnah 4) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:120: Further, there (page 26a), in these words: the "shin" of the tefillin is the supernal Mother, concerning whom it is said (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" - "shin" totals in its letters "shas" [360], the dim Heh of the hand, three hundred sixty-five - and the two hundred forty-eight precepts included in the two hundred forty-eight words of the Shema in the four passages total six hundred thirteen - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:121: Thus far we have summarized from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, relevant to the intent of laying tzitzit and tefillin, and when a person directs his intent in all this, and is solitary by day, and occupies himself with Torah in fear and love with their intents as stated, and directs his intent to the secret of the Name Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs, which is the name of thought, as explained at the beginning of the chapter, he will certainly draw holiness to sanctify his thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:122: And it is good that after laying tallit and tefillin one should direct his intent to the Name Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, which is explained in the Tikkunim (page 9b) as holding the secret of tefillin and tzitzit, in these words: and there is a point in another secret, in the manner of "YHVH Melekh, YHVH Malach, YHVH Yimloch" - Names from above whose points are written beneath them, twelve [permutations] hanging from each and every Name, and concerning them it is said (Isaiah 6:3), "and one called to another" - corresponding to the twelve faces of the three living creatures; "to another" - the twelve wings of the three living creatures, and over them all is the face of man. And the tefillin are the face of man; the tzitzit are the face of the living creatures and the wings of the living creatures. And our Rabbis established there a Name of twelve, that whoever knows it and is careful with it, all his prayers are accepted, and its source is Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - each Yud is the face of YHVH. Aleph - "and each had the face of a man" (Ezekiel 1:10) - here, in this Name, is the secret of tefillin and tzitzit - to this point. And this Name he explained in the Tikkunim, and likewise in other places in the Tikkunim, to be the brain, thought, in the Chokhmah that is in Keter, and it aids in the holiness of thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:123: And this place, explained explicitly (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 100a), I saw fit to copy here, in these words: and this is your lot: "Zarka, Makaf, Shofar, Holech, Segulta" [cantillation marks] - for this stone ascends from your mouth to the place of which it is said, "that which is beyond you, do not inquire, and that which is hidden from you, do not investigate" - and it is the name of the supernal Crown, which is primordial Chokhmah, for "Chokhmah" thus totals the numerical value of the holy Name together with ten letters included in it, which are Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - to this point. And further there: because ten properties of the Name of the Crown descend upon it, which are Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, which are the sefirot full of properties surrounding the supernal crown of the King and the Matronita - and this is the supernal Crown of which it is said, on the day of Sabbath, in the Kedushah, "a crown shall they give You, O LORD our God," and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:124: There are further aspects to the matter of the holiness of thought, and we saw fit to explain them in a chapter of their own, in order to give room between one chapter and the next.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:1: We have already explained, at the beginning of the previous chapter, that the brain and heart are the two primary limbs upon which thought depends, and we explained the matter of the holiness of thought that depends on the brain, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:2: Further, we found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (page 63a), concerning "blessing, holiness, unity," that he explained that they are lion, ox, eagle, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, and three limbs in man corresponding to them: brain, heart, lung, and three accusers corresponding to them: spleen, gall bladder, liver - and upon this chariot rests the supernal face of man, which is the secret of the supernal thought, and this is a good thought, as explained at the beginning of the previous chapter. And there is an evil thought, which is "a worthless man, a man of iniquity" (Proverbs 6:12), "man is like a breath" (Psalms 144:4). And from this you shall see how great a blemish is caused by one who thinks strange thoughts, that he is uprooted from a supernal place to the place of impurity, which is "a worthless man," and so on (Proverbs, ibid.).
